<!--
How to write this (the owner's rule, issue #105, 2026-11-22):
- The general idea first, then each proposal as a small part of its own.
- Every part says what you do, why, how, what you checked before, and the pros and cons. With more than one way, show them and say which one fits our project.
- Technical is fine. But the reader switches between tasks all day: do not assume they remember what you are talking about. Give the context where they need it.
- Code or architecture ideas are welcome, in the same shape.
- Short and to the point. A reader should be able to answer in one line ("ok", or "change part 2").
Delete these notes before you post.
-->

## The general idea
<!-- Two or three sentences: what this is about and where we are. Write it for someone who has not looked at this for a week. -->

## What I checked before proposing
<!-- What you looked at, so nobody has to repeat it: the repo (files, other pages), the mockups, a reference (Bloomy), online research, the docs. One line each, with names and links. -->

---

## Part 1: <name it by what it does>
- **What:** <what will be done>
- **Why:** <the problem it solves; what happens if we do nothing>
- **How:** <the way you will do it; the files, tables or addresses involved; code if it helps>
- **Options:** <the other ways you considered, and which one you recommend for us and why>
- **Pros:** <...>
- **Cons:** <...>

## Part 2: <name>
<!-- Same headings. One part per proposal; if a part has questions, number them and put your suggested answer first. -->

## What I need from you
<!-- The answers that are yours to give, as short as possible. Say what happens if there is no answer ("I use my suggestion"), and what is already decided. -->
